name: Cantilever
summary: A beam or slab fixed at one end that carries load beyond its support, so that it seems to hang in the air.
how: Fix the beam at one end and anchor it with a back span of at least 1 part to every 2 parts of the overhang.
Keep the free end thin; a depth of 1/8 to 1/10 of the span suits steel and concrete.
Repeat the horizontal line in a run of 2 or 3 projecting planes to give a strong shadow.

origin.note: Builders in northern Europe project the upper floors of timber houses beyond the lower floor on jetties.

adoptions.via: Frank Lloyd Wright carries the roofs of the Robie House 6 m past the wall on steel beams.
Mart Stam and then Marcel Breuer bend steel tube into a chair that has no back legs.
The studio block of the Bauhaus Dessau has a small cantilevered balcony at each studio.
The houses of the Weissenhof Estate in Stuttgart extend slabs past their columns, so that the window band can turn the corner.
Marcel Breuer puts the cantilever chair of bent steel tube into series production.
Wright cantilevers the concrete terraces of Fallingwater over a stream in Pennsylvania.
Verner Panton draws the Panton chair as a cantilever seat in one moulded shell.
